requirement:
Project text files MAY use the `{impl}`, `{cite}`, and `{test}` roles with a backtick-delimited full requirement or example name, or with a built-in name under {cite}`requirements.references.builtin_definitions`. A reference MAY instead be written in fenced form, `:::{role} name` on one line, a body, and a closing fence, following the fence rules of {cite}`requirements.ci.span` and {cite}`requirements.ci.fence_lengths`; the fenced form is the same edge with attached commentary, and the inline form carries none. In a source comment, fence lines MUST be recognized after removing each line's comment delimiters within one comment run under {cite}`requirements.references.outline_comments`, and a fence that does not close within its comment run MUST be a validation error. Each reference is a directed edge between its source and the named definition. A source is a project source item or a requirement or example declaration. `{cite}` MUST mean that the source relies on, supports, or refers to the definition, and is an edge from the source to the definition. `{impl}` MUST mean that the source implements part of the definition: it makes a decision, performs a check, produces an output, or handles a case that the definition specifies. A requirement MAY implement part of another requirement by refining one of its obligations. Calling code that implements a definition, or producing a result a caller uses to meet it, MUST NOT by itself count as implementing it. A requirement stating a convention for every output of a kind, such as every validation error, is implemented by the source that carries out the convention as a whole, such as the step that collects and reports those outputs. `{test}` MUST mean that the source is designed to verify behavior the definition specifies: a test through its scenario and the assertions about that scenario's outcome, or a named example through the concrete case it describes. `{impl}` and `{test}` are edges from the definition to the source. Only requirements and examples are assessed; code is reviewed as part of the definitions it implements or tests. Habeas MUST find these references throughout project source files and MUST fail with the source file and line if a name has no matching `{req}` or `{example}` definition. In Markdown, escaped roles and roles in code examples MUST remain literal. Reference discovery MUST consider exactly the project sources that source-access policy permits under {cite}`requirements.authoring.source_tools`: in a Git worktree, files present in the Git index, including staged new files; outside Git, all project files; in both cases excluding the project-root `book` and `evidence` directories, `.git` and `target` directories at any depth, and paths disallowed by {cite}`requirements.configuration.evidence_paths`. Evidence snapshots and generated build output MUST therefore not be counted as source references.

A source item MUST choose its references for each candidate definition by this
procedure, and MAY carry several:

1. If the item is a test or test helper designed to verify the definition, it
   MUST use `{test}`.
2. Otherwise, if fulfilling the definition depends on the item, it MUST use
   `{impl}`. For code, this means it makes a decision, performs a check,
   produces an output, or handles a case the definition specifies. For a type,
   this means the definition constrains its shape: fields, variants, serialized
   form, or validation.
3. Otherwise, if the item should be re-checked or kept in sync when the
   definition changes, it MUST use `{cite}`.
4. If the item carries no reference after applying steps 1 to 3 to every
   definition, it MUST cite the built-in `habeas:none` under
   {cite}`requirements.references.no_requirement`, justifying why the item
   exists.

rationale:
**Judgment: the implementation and tests satisfy `requirements.references.targets`.** I found no unmarked implementation and no untested obligation. I did not run the tests or the code; this rests on reading the marked sources.

**Implementation**

- **Inline roles.** `reference_roles` in `src/lib.rs` finds `{impl}`, `{cite}` and `{test}` with a backtick-delimited name. It accepts a valid full name or a built-in name, and skips escaped roles and roles in Markdown code or raw HTML. It is supported by `protected_ranges`, `is_protected` and `is_escaped`.
- **Fenced roles.** `src/fenced.rs` covers the fenced form:
  - `opening_fence` accepts at least three colons, indentation of at most three spaces, a role, and one valid or built-in name.
  - `find_fences` closes a fence at the next unprotected colon-only line with at least as many colons, so nested fences work.
  - `markdown_fences` and `text_fences` handle Markdown and plain text.
  - `comment_fences` and `strip_comment_delimiters` handle source comments: delimiters are removed per line, fences are matched within one comment run, and each fence gets its run's owning node.
  - `source_fences` dispatches between these cases.
- **Unclosed fences and unknown names.** `validate_references` in `src/evidence.rs` reports a fenced reference that does not close within its comment run or file. It also reports a reference with no matching requirement or example, with file and line. Built-in names resolve through the built-ins check, and a term role is handled separately.
- **Edges.** `SourceReference` and `ReferenceKind` model the three edge kinds. `validate_references` ignores `{cite}` for evidence coverage because it points from the source to the definition, and applies the check to `{impl}` and `{test}`.
- **Discovery.** `collect_references`, `discovered_files` and `collect_references_with_progress` in `src/evidence.rs`, together with `DiscoverySources` in `src/authoring/access.rs`, scan project files:
  - In a Git worktree, discovery covers the indexed files and drops indexed files deleted from the worktree.
  - Outside Git, `walk` covers every file.
  - `excluded_from_discovery` drops `.git` and `target` at any depth, plus root `book` and `evidence`.
  - `considers` applies `[evidence]` disallow rules and the credentials exclusion.
  - Symlinks are not followed, and binary files are skipped.
- **Reference procedure (steps 1–4).** The `{test}`/`{impl}`/`{cite}`/`habeas:none` selection procedure is an authoring convention. Other requirements enforce it (`rust_item_coverage`, `no_requirement`, `citation_review`), so I did not reassess it here.
- **`{impl}` marking.** The helpers I read carry `{impl}` on this requirement or on the requirement they actually serve. Examples are `colon_fence` (`ci.span`, `ci.fence_lengths`), `valid_name` (`ci.identifiers`), `justification` (`no_requirement`), `MarkdownFence` (`book_badges`) and `untracked` (`cli.status`). I found no unmarked implementation of this requirement and no behavior the requirement does not specify.

**Tests**

- **Fence parsing (`src/fenced.rs`).**
  - `opening_fences_take_a_role_and_one_valid_or_built_in_name` covers valid and invalid openings, four-space indentation, bad names, the `habeas:` prefix and a fence with too few colons.
  - `markdown_fences_close_with_enough_colons_and_skip_code` covers nesting, a fence that never closes, and code-block protection.
  - `comment_delimiters_are_removed_per_line` covers delimiter stripping.
  - `comment_fences_close_within_one_comment_run` covers a later run not closing an earlier fence, block comments, and the owning node.
- **Literals.** `src/lib.rs` has two tests, `markdown_examples_and_escaped_references_stay_literal` (escapes, escaped backslashes and code) and `references_in_requirement_bodies_are_scanned_as_markdown`. `every_markdown_extension_keeps_escaped_and_code_roles_literal` in `src/evidence.rs` covers literals across the `.md`, `.markdown`, `.MD` and `.Markdown` extensions, with a `.txt` control.
- **Discovery.**
  - `discovery_considers_indexed_files_except_exclusions_and_credentials` (`src/authoring/access.rs`) covers a staged file, a deleted file, an untracked file, nested `target`, root `evidence`, a nested `book` directory and a credentials file.
  - `reference_discovery_skips_evidence_snapshots_and_build_output` (`src/evidence.rs`) covers the root and nested `book` and `evidence` directories, `target`, `.git` and binary files.
  - `disallowed_paths_are_skipped_and_projects_outside_git_scan_every_file` (`tests/references.rs`) covers disallow rules and projects outside Git.
  - `untracked_sources_are_not_validated_until_staged_and_status_lists_them` (`tests/references.rs`) covers the staging boundary.
  - `references_report_only_sites_in_considered_sources` (`src/authoring/tools.rs`) covers the same rules through the `references` tool.
- **Validation failures.**
  - `reports_unknown_references_and_uncovered_lines` checks the file:line error for an unknown name and the uncovered-reference error.
  - `fenced_references_in_comments_and_built_in_rules_are_validated` checks the unclosed-fence error, built-in role and form errors, and fenced references in comments.
  - `uncovered_cite_is_not_reported_while_uncovered_impl_and_test_are` checks the edge semantics: `{cite}` needs no input coverage, while `{impl}` and `{test}` do.
- **Authoring inputs.** The `src/authoring/inputs.rs` tests check that `{impl}` and `{test}` edges leaving the subject become inputs and that `{cite}` edges do not.

No FIXME or other acknowledged gaps appear in the sources. Not exercised directly: root `book` exclusion in Git mode (the Git-mode test covers only nested `book`; `book` is covered outside Git), and a tracked symlink. Both use simple, shared code paths, so I do not count them as gaps.

{test}`requirements.references.targets`
:::{req} builtin_definitions
Habeas MUST provide built-in definitions named `habeas:<name>`, available in
every project without a declaration. Each built-in MUST have fixed text, which
states its obligations and is documented in Habeas's reference documentation, and
MUST state which reference roles may use it. References MUST resolve built-in
names alongside project definitions. So that every book stands alone, the book
MUST render a reference to a built-in as a badge without a link whose hover text
gives the built-in's full text. Built-ins MUST NOT require or permit evidence
files and MUST NOT appear in the requirements index, `habeas status`, or the
missing-evidence check of {cite}`requirements.ci.coverage`. A project definition
MUST NOT use a full name beginning with `habeas:`; validation MUST report one,
and the `:` character already makes such names invalid under
{cite}`requirements.ci.identifiers`. Validation MUST report a reference to a
built-in in a role the built-in does not permit, or that breaks the built-in's
stated form.
:::{req} span

A `{req}` definition MUST use an opening fence of at least three colons immediately followed by `{req} <name>`. A closing fence MUST have at least as many colons as the opening fence and nothing else on its line except whitespace. As in CommonMark fences, an opening or closing fence MAY be indented by up to three spaces; a line indented by four or more spaces MUST NOT be a fence. The requirement body MUST be all Markdown between those fence lines, including headings, examples, diagrams, and blank lines, and MUST NOT include text after the closing fence. Leading and trailing whitespace MUST be excluded when comparing the body with evidence.
:::{req} fence_lengths

A `{req}` opening fence MAY contain four or more colons. Habeas MUST accept opening fences of any length of at least three colons. A colon-only line with fewer colons than the opener MUST remain inside the requirement body, allowing a nested colon directive. A closing fence outside a fenced code example with at least as many colons as the opener MUST end the body.
:::{req} outline_comments
Each documented profile defines which grammar nodes are comments; the Markdown
profile's comments are HTML comment blocks, so an inline HTML comment within a
paragraph is text of its section. In every supported language, comments on consecutive lines with no other source
between them MUST form one comment run. A comment that follows other source on
the same line, including another comment, MUST form a run by itself and MUST belong to the innermost outline node
containing that line. Any other run MUST belong to the next outline node that
starts after it within the smallest node containing it; when that container has
no such node, the run MUST belong to the container, which is the root node at top
level. A profile MAY bind a comment kind to its container
instead: such a run MUST belong to the smallest node containing it. The Rust
profile MUST bind inner doc comments (`//!`, `/*!`) to their container, so a
file-level inner doc comment belongs to the root node. A reference in a comment MUST count for the node its run belongs to under
{cite}`requirements.references.rust_item_coverage` and
{cite}`requirements.references.authoring_inputs`.
:::{req} source_tools
The harness MUST expose a `habeas` tool accepting exactly one of these request
forms. Each form MUST correspond to one existing evidence-input kind:
| Request fields | Evidence input returned | Definition |
| `file: String`, `line_start: Integer`, optional `line_end: Integer` | Outline inputs for the innermost outline nodes covering the range | {cite}`requirements.ci.outline_inputs` |
| `file: String`, `item: String` | Outline input | {cite}`requirements.ci.outline_inputs` |
| `requirements: String` | Requirements input, including its matching names | {cite}`requirements.ci.requirements_inputs` |
| `definition: String` | Definition input | {cite}`requirements.definitions.inputs` |
Selector arguments MUST use the syntax defined by
{cite}`requirements.references.outline_selectors`. Reads MUST use the current
project working tree, including unstaged changes to tracked files and staged new
files. By default, source inputs MUST stay within the project root after
resolving symlinks; in a Git worktree, both the requested file and its resolved
target MUST be present in the Git index. Projects outside Git MUST use the same
containment rules without requiring an index. Failure to read an existing
repository's index MUST be reported as an error.
The project-root `evidence/` directory and an active workspace configuration
containing literal credentials MUST be excluded from model reads by default,
including symlink aliases. Generated build outputs MUST follow
{cite}`requirements.authoring.generated_inputs`. Workspace path overrides MUST
follow {cite}`requirements.configuration.evidence_paths`, including explicit
permission for otherwise excluded inputs. A denied mandatory input or explicit
read MUST abort under {cite}`requirements.authoring.read_denial`.
Line numbers are only a way to request sources; recorded evidence MUST identify
sources by outline selector and structural hash, never by line number. Request
line numbers MUST be one-based and inclusive, and omitting `line_end` MUST read
through EOF. A line-range request MUST be resolved to the innermost outline
nodes covering the requested lines, which are `line` nodes in a file using the
plain-text profile; the result MUST show the model each node's selector, current
line range, and source text, and the harness MUST record those nodes as outline
inputs. The model-facing tool description MUST include the argument conventions
from the cited requirements, including outline selector syntax, definition
selections, and full definition names, with a short request example for each form.
A successful call MUST return the requested evidence input, populated by the
harness with the selected source text, using the existing evidence schema.
{cite}`requirements.ci.schema`
Required terminology dependencies MUST be returned alongside it as additional
definition inputs under {cite}`requirements.definitions.authoring_inputs`.
The result MUST have this shape:
```text
HabeasResult {
input: EvidenceInput,
definitions: Array<DefinitionInput>,
`definitions` MUST be empty when no additional terminology is required. The
harness MUST record inputs supplied to the model in the assessment's evidence.
A failed read MUST add no evidence input. Access-policy denials MUST abort
except where {cite}`requirements.authoring.read_denial` makes them ordinary read
failures; other failed reads MUST return an explanatory tool error.
:::{req} evidence_paths
The workspace `[evidence]` table MUST serialize EvidenceConfig. `allow` and
`disallow` MUST be arrays of nonempty literal paths, each naming a file or a
directory subtree. Relative paths MUST resolve from the selected `habeas.toml`
directory; absolute paths MUST be supported. These paths are not glob patterns.
An omitted `allow` or `disallow` MUST mean an empty array, and an absent
`[evidence]` table MUST mean both are empty, so only the default source-access
rules apply. No operation requires the section. The table has no user-file
counterpart, and these rules have no invocation options. This section refines
{impl}`requirements.configuration.feature_sections` for the evidence feature.
For authoring reads, a matching disallow MUST reject the path; otherwise a
matching allow MUST permit it; otherwise the default source-access rules MUST
apply. Explicit allow MUST override every default, including Git tracking,
project containment, generated-evidence exclusion, and automatic generated-output
rules. Disallow MUST win even when an allow or generated-output rule also matches.
Both the requested path and its resolved symlink target MUST be checked for
disallow, so an allowed alias cannot expose a disallowed target.
The same explicit disallow rules and external-path exceptions MUST apply when
resolving recorded evidence inputs, including ordinary validation and
`add-input`. Validation MUST remain independent of Git index membership: it
checks the recorded inputs' existence and contents. Loading path policy MUST NOT
resolve credentials or validate unused authoring settings.
:::{req} no_requirement
Habeas MUST provide the built-in `habeas:none` under
{cite}`requirements.references.builtin_definitions`, with this text:
> Cite this only when no requirement or example applies to the item under the
> reference procedure. The citation MUST use the fenced form, and its body MUST
> justify why the item exists. An item with an invariant worth checking, such as
> a cache that must not change results, needs a requirement stating that
> invariant instead. An item citing this MUST NOT implement end-user-observable
> behavior that no requirement specifies.
Only `{cite}` MAY reference it. Validation MUST report an inline citation of it
or a fenced citation whose body, without comment delimiters and other
references, is empty. Whether the justification holds MUST be assessed under
{cite}`requirements.references.citation_review`. `habeas status --all` MUST list
each `habeas:none` citation with its item and justification.
